raw_text: Publish a fixed candidate when ready for independent review. Suggested area: django/db/migrations/serializer.py (TypeSerializer / type resolution for nested classes) and a regression test in tests/migrations/test_writer.py covering a classmethod default defined on a nested TextChoices class. Notify me with handoff_patch including the patch_id so I can integrate_patch, run_tests on that exact version, and record an accept/request-changes review.

Final candidate for independent review: patch-1 (source version v6, 2 changed paths).

What it fixes (issue: "Class methods from nested classes cannot be used as Field.default"):
- django/db/migrations/serializer.py — FunctionTypeSerializer builds a bound classmethod reference as "<module>.<klass>.<method>". It used klass.__name__, which for a nested class yields the non-resolvable "appname.models.Capability.default". Now uses klass.__qualname__, producing the correct "appname.models.Profile.Capability.default". Top-level classes are unaffected (qualname == name).
- tests/migrations/test_writer.py — added module-level TestModel2 with nested Capability(models.TextChoices) exposing a @classmethod default(), plus regression test test_serialize_nested_class_method asserting MigrationWriter.serialize(TestModel2.Capability.default) == "migrations.test_writer.TestModel2.Capability.default" with imports {"import migrations.test_writer"}.

Evidence I obtained on this exact version (v6): django migrations.test_writer => 54 collected, 54 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (validation_status verified); focused run of test_serialize_nested_class_method + test_serialize_functions => 2/2 passed. An earlier intermediate attempt using a locally defined class failed as expected (local qualnames contain "<locals>") and was replaced by the module-level model.

Please integrate_patch patch-1 into your own tree, run the public tests on that exact version, and record accept or request-changes. My workspace has no further edits after patch-1, so patch-1 is my exact final candidate.

Review decision recorded: ACCEPT for patch-1 (review-1).

Evidence: I adopted patch-1 into my private tree (integrate_patch → source v2, files_sha256 2e374d76…, no conflicts) and ran the public Django tests on that exact version: {"kind":"django","targets":["migrations.test_writer"]} → 54 collected / 54 passed, 0 failed, validation_status verified (report test-report-a3d0c609fc12544c882b51a8, test event sequence 32).

Code review: FunctionTypeSerializer now emits module + klass.__qualname__ + method, so a classmethod on a nested TextChoices class serializes as "appname.models.Profile.Capability.default" (the expected value) instead of the unresolvable "appname.models.Capability.default". Top-level classes are unaffected (qualname == name). The regression test asserts both the string and the single module import.

Next, for you (delivery member): integrate patch-1 into your tree if not already, run_tests on that exact final version (both public groups), fix_patch(task_ids=[]) if your current version differs, and submit_integration. No rework requested from my side.
